page: OVHcloud r2-60 is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The processor lacks hyperthreading and TSX instructions, but supports AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA. It is configured with 60.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the r2-60 is positioned in the lower tiers for compute-intensive tasks. Single-core stress-ng performance is in the bottom 10% with a score of 868.79, while multi-core performance falls in the bottom 25% at 3118.23. Geekbench scores align with this, showing a single-core score of 976.0 and a multi-core score of 2991.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a weak to poor profile, with uncached large-block read speeds at 19.87 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.43 GB/sec. However, the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating of 1967.54, reflecting stable memory access capabilities despite the older CPU architecture.

The primary tradeoff of the r2-60 is its reliance on older Intel Haswell hardware, which limits its raw processing power and memory throughput compared to modern architectures. However, this hardware profile offers a qualitatively cost-effective solution for workloads requiring high memory capacity without demanding high CPU performance. With 60 GB of RAM and dedicated vCPUs, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, Redis deployments, lightweight database hosting, and moderate web serving.

It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 60.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 100 GB SSD. The server delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.0 GB per core, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require high-performance compute. Benchmark results show weak compute performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2991.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 4424.99, though its Passmark memory score remains average. This hardware configuration is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, Redis deployments, and lightweight database hosting.
